scope: Strategy-to-rule research routing for common stock and option structures. The catalog identifies facts, evidence, and rule families to investigate; it does not choose a trade, determine a filing position, or calculate liability.
disclaimer: General educational information only. Tax treatment is fact-dependent, state and local rules differ, and the taxpayer's complete return, elections, basis history, other accounts, and year-end forms may change the result.
agentOutputContract: State the strategy, account context, jurisdiction, and review date.
Separate broker-observed facts, user-supplied facts, official tax rules, planning inferences, and facts not evaluated.
List every material missing fact before describing a possible tax consequence.
Do not infer tax treatment from a strategy name, ticker, OCC symbol, app estimate, or order label alone.
Do not calculate personalized tax liability or claim that a structure is tax-efficient without the taxpayer's complete facts.
Tax research never authorizes a trade, roll, assignment response, lot selection, or account change.

strategies.title: Covered call and buy-write
strategies.summary: Route stock plus a written call through option-writer recognition, qualified-covered-call rules, dividend holding periods, lot basis, constructive-sale screening, and broker reporting.

supplementalClaims.text: For common-stock qualified-dividend treatment, Publication 550 generally requires more than 60 holding days during the 121-day window beginning 60 days before the ex-dividend date.

Days generally do not count toward that dividend holding period while risk of loss is diminished, including certain periods when the taxpayer grants an option to buy substantially identical stock; qualified-covered-call rules can affect the analysis.

requiredFacts.prompt: Is the position in a taxable account, traditional IRA, Roth IRA, or another account type?
requiredFacts.why: Current recognition and available broker records differ by account.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which stock lots are covered, including acquisition dates, quantities, adjusted basis, and basis provenance?
requiredFacts.why: Stock holding period, assignment proceeds, dividend qualification, and lot identification depend on the actual lots.

requiredFacts.prompt: What are the exact call instrument, strike, expiration, quantity, premium, and lifecycle dates?
requiredFacts.why: Qualified-covered-call and writer treatment cannot be inferred from the label covered call.

requiredFacts.prompt: Did the stock pay a dividend, and which holding days involved diminished risk?
requiredFacts.why: Dividend qualification has a separate holding-period test.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were there other calls, puts, shorts, forwards, collars, or substantially related positions?
requiredFacts.why: Straddle and constructive-sale analysis depends on the complete position.

brokerReads.purpose: Resolve the owned account and account class.
Read exact stock lots and basis availability.
Read the exact short-call contract and position side.
Reconcile fills, assignments, exercises, and expirations.
Reconcile official year-end reporting.

workflow: Classify the exact stock lots and call contract.
Determine whether qualified-covered-call status is supported, unsupported, or not evaluable.
Analyze option recognition, stock basis, assignment proceeds, and dividend holding period separately.
Report broker estimates and federal rule research in separate evidence lanes.
Leave the filing result unevaluated when contract, lot, dividend, or related-position facts are incomplete.
redFlags: Deep-in-the-money or long-dated call without a qualified-covered-call analysis.
Dividend qualification asserted from Form 1099-DIV alone.
Covered-call label used to dismiss constructive-sale or straddle questions.
Assignment discussed without identifying delivered stock lots and premium adjustment.
stopConditions: Additional offsetting positions are not represented in the account evidence.
Transferred basis, corporate actions, or selected-lot confirmation is missing.
The user asks for a definitive dividend, loss, or filing conclusion.

strategies.title: Cash-secured put
strategies.summary: Route a short put through option-writer recognition, assignment basis, replacement-property review, retirement-account interactions, and year-end reporting.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which account holds the put, and are related acquisitions occurring in any taxable or retirement account?
requiredFacts.why: Replacement acquisitions in retirement accounts can have different consequences.

requiredFacts.prompt: What are the exact put instrument, strike, expiration, premium, quantity, and lifecycle events?
requiredFacts.why: Expiration, closing purchase, and assignment have different mechanics.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were substantially identical shares, options, or contracts sold at a loss in the surrounding 61-day window?
requiredFacts.why: Assignment or a replacement option may interact with wash-sale rules.

requiredFacts.prompt: If assigned, what shares were acquired and what premium, fees, date, and broker basis were recorded?
requiredFacts.why: Written-put premium generally adjusts acquired-stock basis.

brokerReads.purpose: Resolve account class and ownership.
Read the exact short-put holding and contract identifiers.
Read assignment, expiration, exercise, and option-event evidence.
Read resulting or replacement stock lots.

workflow: Identify whether the put expired, was closed, or was assigned.
Treat the option result and acquired-stock basis as separate outputs.
Scan taxable, retirement, recurring, and DRIP activity for replacement acquisitions.
Do not label a replacement option safe solely from strike or expiration differences.
Reconcile to year-end forms before a filing conclusion.
redFlags: Premium described as taxable when received rather than at the lifecycle event.
Assignment basis computed without written premium.
Wash-sale review limited to one account or only identical ticker purchases.
IRA or Roth IRA acquisition ignored after a taxable-account loss.
stopConditions: Other brokers, spouse accounts, or automatic acquisitions are unknown.
Substantially-identical treatment depends on unresolved option facts.
The user asks for a definitive wash-sale or basis filing result.

strategies.title: Wheel strategy
strategies.summary: Treat the wheel as a sequence of separate option events and stock lots, not one continuous tax object.

requiredFacts.prompt: What are the open, close, expiration, assignment, exercise, and stock-sale events for every leg?
requiredFacts.why: Each leg can realize or defer a different item.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which assigned or purchased stock lots remain, and which lots were delivered or sold?
requiredFacts.why: Basis, holding period, lot identification, and assignment proceeds require exact lots.

requiredFacts.prompt: What same-underlying activity occurred across taxable, retirement, recurring, and DRIP accounts during each loss window?
requiredFacts.why: Repeated cycles can create replacement acquisitions around realized losses.

requiredFacts.prompt: Did held stock pay dividends while calls were open, and were the calls technically qualified covered calls?
requiredFacts.why: Dividend and stock holding-period effects are separate from option premium recognition.

brokerReads.purpose: Classify the current wheel stage from actual stock and option holdings.
Build the event ledger across equities and options.
Read remaining and disposed stock lots.
Read option lifecycle and assignment events.
Check recurring activity that can create replacement shares.

workflow: Expand the wheel into a dated event ledger.
Analyze each closed or expired option separately from assigned or sold shares.
Track stock basis and holding period from the actual assignment or purchase date.
Run wash-sale and retirement-account checks around every realized loss.
Treat projected wheel income as economic analysis, not current taxable income.
redFlags: Net premium across many legs presented as the taxable result.
Rolls treated as automatically deferring recognition.
Assigned shares treated as inheriting the option holding period.
Covered calls assumed qualified without contract analysis.
Recurring buys or DRIP ignored during a harvesting window.
stopConditions: The event ledger cannot reconcile order history to stock lots.
Activity at another broker or retirement account is unknown.
The user asks whether the whole strategy is categorically tax-efficient.

strategies.title: Equity-option roll
strategies.summary: A roll is a close and a new open. Analyze the closed contract and replacement contract separately.

requiredFacts.prompt: What exact contract, side, position effect, quantity, fill, and date closed?
requiredFacts.why: The close leg is a separate realization event.

requiredFacts.prompt: What exact replacement contract, strike, expiration, quantity, fill, and date opened?
requiredFacts.why: Replacement exposure drives wash-sale and straddle review.

requiredFacts.prompt: Was the option long or written, covered or uncovered, and linked to stock or other offsets?
requiredFacts.why: Recognition, QCC, and offsetting-position rules differ by role.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were related contracts or shares acquired in another taxable or retirement account?
requiredFacts.why: One-account evidence is not a complete wash-sale review.

brokerReads.purpose: Read exact option fills and order linkage.
Read remaining option holdings after the roll.
Preserve staged cash-account roll intent without claiming execution.

workflow: Decompose net roll price into closed and opened contracts.
Do not infer deferral from continued economic exposure.
Flag wash-sale, straddle, or QCC review only when facts support the flag.
Keep order evidence separate from a roll ledger or UI description.
Report missing cross-account facts as not evaluated.
redFlags: Roll described as tax-free or deferred because it was one broker ticket.
Net debit or credit used as the tax result without separate legs.
Changed strike or expiration treated as a universal wash-sale escape.
Roll ledger treated as proof the open leg executed.
stopConditions: Close and open fills cannot be separated.
Original contract basis or written premium is missing.
Substantially-identical or straddle treatment requires a personalized conclusion.

strategies.title: Tax-loss harvesting and replacement exposure
strategies.summary: Route a loss sale through exact-lot identification, a complete 61-day acquisition review, retirement-account checks, and post-trade reconciliation.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which exact lot would be sold, with adjusted basis, acquisition date, quantity, and unrealized loss?
requiredFacts.why: Harvesting is lot-specific.

requiredFacts.prompt: What related stock, option, recurring, DRIP, spouse, and other-broker acquisitions occurred or are scheduled in the 61-day window?
requiredFacts.why: The statutory window reaches before and after the sale and can cross accounts.

requiredFacts.prompt: What replacement exposure is proposed, and what supports or undermines substantially-identical treatment?
requiredFacts.why: There is no universal option-strike or expiration safe harbor.

requiredFacts.prompt: What realized gains, carryovers, elections, and return-year facts are relevant?
requiredFacts.why: The economic value of a loss cannot be calculated from one lot alone.

brokerReads.purpose: Read exact available lots and basis provenance.
Read filled sales and acquisitions around the window.
Read automatic recurring acquisitions.
Read DRIP and related account settings.
Reconcile official tax documents after year end.

workflow: Identify the exact loss lot before discussing replacement exposure.
Build a 61-day acquisition ledger across all known accounts and automations.
Classify replacements as clearly identical, clearly different, or fact-specific.
Leave estimated tax value unevaluated without return-wide facts.
After execution, verify the filled lot and reconcile broker adjustments.
redFlags: Position-level loss used instead of a selected lot.
Only the 30 days after sale reviewed.
IRA, Roth IRA, spouse, DRIP, recurring, or other-broker acquisitions omitted.
Replacement option declared safe solely because strike or expiration changed.
App estimate treated as the final wash-sale adjustment.
stopConditions: The complete acquisition ledger is unavailable.
Transferred basis or corporate-action adjustments are unresolved.
The user asks for a definitive substantially-identical or tax-savings conclusion.

strategies.title: Section 1256 index-option structure
strategies.summary: Confirm the actual contract before applying Section 1256, then analyze mark-to-market, 60/40 character, Form 6781, straddles, elections, and reporting separately.

requiredFacts.prompt: What exact contract, underlying index, exchange product, exercise style, settlement, and broker classification are involved?
requiredFacts.why: The phrase index option or a ticker does not establish statutory status.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which qualifying contracts remained open on the last business day of the tax year?
requiredFacts.why: Section 1256 generally marks qualifying open contracts to market annually.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were the contracts part of a mixed straddle, hedge, box, collar, or position with non-Section-1256 legs?
requiredFacts.why: Mixed positions and elections can change the simple result.

requiredFacts.prompt: What did the broker report for the return year, and were Form 6781 elections or adjustments made?
requiredFacts.why: Transaction history alone is not the complete filing record.

brokerReads.purpose: Resolve exact option contract and product metadata.
Read current and historical option events.
Read official tax forms and Section 1256 reporting.

workflow: Confirm contract identity before applying Section 1256 language.
Separate 60/40 capital character from marginal-rate comparisons.
Identify year-end open contracts and mark-to-market items.
Screen for mixed straddles, hedges, boxes, and elections.
Reconcile to Form 1099-B and Form 6781.
redFlags: Any index option assumed Section 1256 from ticker alone.
60/40 described as a tax rate rather than character.
Open year-end contracts omitted.
Mixed equity and Section 1256 legs treated as a pure Section 1256 position.
stopConditions: Contract classification or broker reporting is unavailable.
A mixed-straddle or election question is material.
The user asks for a personalized rate advantage.

strategies.title: Box spread and fixed-return option structure
strategies.summary: A fixed payoff does not create one automatic tax characterization. Analyze contract identity, Section 1256, straddles, conversion transactions, elections, purpose, and reporting.

requiredFacts.prompt: What are the exact four contracts, expirations, strikes, quantities, fills, settlement style, and product classifications?
requiredFacts.why: Contract composition controls Section 1256 and mixed-position questions.

requiredFacts.prompt: Was the structure entered for investment, financing, hedging, or another purpose?
requiredFacts.why: Conversion-transaction and interest-equivalent analysis can depend on purpose and economics.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were there related appreciated positions, hedges, straddles, or offsetting contracts?
requiredFacts.why: The box may not be analyzable in isolation.

requiredFacts.prompt: What elections and return-year reporting apply?
requiredFacts.why: Form 6781 and mixed-straddle elections can change timing and character.

brokerReads.purpose: Inspect each exact option contract and settlement characteristic.
Inspect required inputs for non-sending package analysis.
Reconcile year-end Section 1256 and straddle reporting.

workflow: Verify the four exact contracts and statutory classification of each leg.
Separate fixed economic payoff from federal timing and character.
Screen for straddle, conversion-transaction, constructive-sale, and election issues.
Treat financing-cost or favorable-character claims as fact-specific inferences.
Require professional review before a personalized deduction or characterization.
redFlags: Short-box cost called automatically deductible interest or capital loss.
Long-box return called automatically favorable 60/40 income.
Mixed contracts treated as a pure Section 1256 box.
Execution and settlement risk dismissed because payoff is fixed at expiration.
stopConditions: Any leg's statutory classification is unclear.
The structure is linked to another appreciated or offsetting position.
The user requests a definitive financing deduction or filing characterization.

strategies.title: Collar or protective-put structure
strategies.summary: Route stock hedges through actual risk retained, exact contracts, stock lots, constructive sales, straddles, qualified-covered-call status, dividends, and reporting.

supplementalClaims.text: Publication 550 says qualified-dividend holding days generally exclude periods in which risk of loss is diminished by a put, a granted call on substantially identical stock, a short sale, or similar related positions, subject to applicable exceptions and regulations.

requiredFacts.prompt: What exact stock lots, holding periods, basis, and unrealized appreciation are hedged?
requiredFacts.why: Constructive-sale and holding-period analysis depends on the appreciated lots.

requiredFacts.prompt: What are the exact put and call strikes, expirations, quantities, premiums, and exercise styles?
requiredFacts.why: Strategy labels do not show how much market risk remains.

requiredFacts.prompt: What market risk remains after considering every related position and obligation?
requiredFacts.why: Constructive-sale and straddle questions turn on actual offset.

requiredFacts.prompt: Did dividends occur while the hedge diminished risk?
requiredFacts.why: Qualified-dividend holding days can be affected separately from stock gain recognition.

brokerReads.purpose: Read stock lots and unrealized appreciation.
Read every exact option leg and position side.
Read dividend dates and holding-linked payouts.

workflow: Identify appreciated stock lots and every hedge leg.
Measure actual risk retained without converting the measurement into a tax conclusion.
Screen constructive-sale, straddle, QCC, stock, and dividend holding-period rules separately.
Classify unsupported conclusions as not evaluated or fact-specific.
Keep hedge research separate from trade authorization.
redFlags: Collar label used as proof that Section 1259 does or does not apply.
Qualified-dividend status assumed despite diminished risk.
Only one leg considered while another related position remains open.
Tax treatment inferred from net zero premium.
stopConditions: The complete related-position set is unknown.
Actual risk retained cannot be established.
The user requests a definitive constructive-sale conclusion.

strategies.title: Dividend capture or short holding-period dividend trade
strategies.summary: Route a short holding-period dividend trade through qualified-dividend eligibility, diminished-risk days, payments in lieu, stock-lot results, and Form 1099-DIV reconciliation.

supplementalClaims.text: For common stock, Publication 550 generally requires holding the shares for more than 60 days during the 121-day period beginning 60 days before the ex-dividend date for qualified-dividend treatment.

The holding-day count generally excludes days when risk of loss is diminished by a put, an open short sale, a granted call on substantially identical stock, or substantially similar or related positions.
Payments in lieu of dividends are not automatically qualified dividends, and dividends tied to related-payment obligations can be excluded from qualified-dividend treatment.

requiredFacts.prompt: What were the stock trade dates, ex-dividend date, record date, and disposition date?
requiredFacts.why: Qualified-dividend eligibility uses a specific holding window and day count.

requiredFacts.prompt: Were puts, calls, short sales, forwards, collars, or related positions open during the window?
requiredFacts.why: Those days may not count toward the holding requirement.

requiredFacts.prompt: Was the payment an issuer dividend or a payment in lieu, and how was it reported?
requiredFacts.why: Payment labels can differ from qualified-dividend treatment.

requiredFacts.prompt: Was the stock sold at a loss, and were extraordinary or other distributions received?
requiredFacts.why: Separate loss-character or basis rules may apply.

brokerReads.purpose: Read stock acquisition and disposition history.
Read exact stock lots and holding dates.
Read dividends and payable dates.
Reconcile Form 1099-DIV and payment classification.

workflow: Build the holding-day timeline using trade and ex-dividend dates.
Exclude diminished-risk days only when supported by complete facts.
Distinguish issuer dividends from payments in lieu and related-payment obligations.
Separate dividend character from economic profit and stock gain or loss.
Do not call a trade tax-advantaged from displayed dividend amounts alone.
redFlags: Form 1099-DIV box 1b treated as conclusive despite a failed holding-period test.
Options or hedges ignored while counting holding days.
Payment in lieu described as a qualified dividend.
Dividend amount discussed without the stock price and disposition result.
stopConditions: Trade dates, ex-dividend date, or risk-diminishing positions are incomplete.
Payment classification cannot be reconciled to the tax form.
The user asks for a personalized tax-rate or after-tax-return conclusion.

strategies.title: Short stock and substantially identical long property
strategies.summary: Route a short sale through closing-property character, substantially identical long positions, holding-period effects, wash sales, payments, constructive sales, and reporting.

supplementalClaims.text: Section 1233 can treat gain on a short sale as short-term and can restart the holding period of substantially identical property held or acquired during the short sale, subject to its statutory conditions.

If substantially identical property had been held for more than one year on the short-sale date, Section 1233 can treat a loss on closing the short sale as long-term, subject to its scope and exceptions.
Related payments and payments in lieu of dividends require separate classification and are not automatically qualified dividends.

requiredFacts.prompt: What property was sold short, when was it opened and closed, and what property closed it?
requiredFacts.why: Character and timing depend on the short-sale lifecycle and closing property.

requiredFacts.prompt: What substantially identical stock, securities, futures, or puts were held or acquired?
requiredFacts.why: Section 1233 rules depend on substantially identical property.

requiredFacts.prompt: Was the short economically offsetting an appreciated financial position?
requiredFacts.why: Short-against-the-box structures can raise constructive-sale questions.

requiredFacts.prompt: What dividends, payments in lieu, and related-payment obligations occurred?
requiredFacts.why: Payment character is separate from short-sale gain or loss.

brokerReads.purpose: Read short-position and closing transaction history where supported.
Read related long stock lots.
Reconcile payments and official tax forms.

workflow: Build the short-sale open and close timeline.
Inventory substantially identical property held or acquired during the short.
Apply Section 1233 separately from wash-sale and constructive-sale review.
Classify dividend-related payments from official records.
Leave unsupported deduction and filing conclusions unevaluated.
redFlags: Short-sale gain assumed long-term from the holding period of delivered shares.
Existing long property ignored.
Short against the box described as deferring gain without Section 1259 review.
Payment in lieu described as an ordinary qualified dividend.
stopConditions: The closing property or substantially identical holdings are unknown.
Spouse, other-broker, or derivative activity may be material but unavailable.
The user asks for a definitive deduction, character, or constructive-sale conclusion.

strategies.title: Specific-lot stock sale
strategies.summary: Route a lot-aware sale through timely identification, written confirmation, basis provenance, holding period, fallback, wash-sale adjustments, and post-fill verification.

requiredFacts.prompt: Which exact lots are available, including quantity, acquisition date, adjusted basis, basis source, and holding period?
requiredFacts.why: A position-level average cannot substitute for selected shares.

requiredFacts.prompt: When and how will the broker receive the instruction, and what confirmation will be retained?
requiredFacts.why: Adequate identification depends on timely instruction and confirmation.

requiredFacts.prompt: What default method applies if selected shares are unavailable or the instruction fails?
requiredFacts.why: Executed lots can differ from the plan.

requiredFacts.prompt: Are transferred basis, corporate actions, return of capital, wash sales, or missing adjustments unresolved?
requiredFacts.why: Displayed basis can be incomplete or estimated.

brokerReads.purpose: Inventory exact open lots and basis provenance.
Build a non-sending exact-lot plan.
Verify the order and selected or closed lots after execution.
Reconcile year-end basis and proceeds.

workflow: Read current eligible lots immediately before planning.
Preserve selected lot IDs, quantities, basis provenance, and expected fallback.
Keep the plan non-sending until exact approval and a verified live contract are available.
After the fill, verify order history and the broker lot record.
Reconcile to year-end forms and external basis records.
redFlags: Average cost used as if it were a specific lot.
A planning screen treated as confirmation or execution evidence.
Unavailable selected shares silently replaced by a different lot.
Transferred or missing basis ignored.
Lot selection optimized without return-wide facts.
stopConditions: The selected lot is unavailable or basis provenance is unresolved.
The broker cannot provide retained confirmation of the instruction.
The user asks which lot minimizes tax without return-wide facts.
